body.statement: Let \(\Phi\) forget only the explicit serialization and supplied decomposition while retaining the canonical variables, equalities, and objective. For every fixed \(q,k\), \(\Phi(\mathfrak I_{q,k}^{\ge3})\subsetneq\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{SI}}\cap\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{D}}\): inclusion follows from canonical semantics, and it is proper because both published admissible classes permit nonrational tables and programs with scalar width exceeding \(k\), while the Duarte et al. class additionally permits broader discrete causal structures. The headline image is not contained in \(\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{SI}}^{\le2}\), and \(\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{SI}}^{\le2}\) is not contained in \(\Phi(\mathfrak I_{q,k}^{\ge3})\); the first family contains genuine degree-at-least-three objectives and the second contains one- and two-component objectives excluded by the headline cardinality condition. Thus the exact-width theorem is a strict guarantee improvement only on the common explicit bounded-width image, not a subsumption of either comparator's full admissible program class.
body.justification: The guarantee comparison is meaningful only after the proposed serialized class is located exactly inside the published admissible program domains.
body.gap: The comparator papers do not formulate the explicit scalar equality-and-objective width subclass, so neither their broad admissibility nor their low-degree tractability statement supplies this inclusion audit.
body.consumer: A referee can distinguish a strict guarantee improvement on a common subclass from a false claim that bounded scalar width covers every published causal program.
